cards.title: Equities: Tariff Proposal Lands on a War Market
cards.body: The S&P 500 stands at {SPX} and the Nasdaq at {NDX}. On 25 November the US Trade Representative proposed tariffs of up to 20% on 14 economies, including China, the EU, Japan and South Korea, after a probe into excess capacity; US stocks fell on the news, Reuters reported via Al Jazeera. The rates go to public comment, with action possible in January, and China says it reserves the right to respond. Oil risk has not gone away: Brent trades at {BRENT} after Houthi claims on Saudi ports and a refinery.

cards.title: Oil: Gulf Exports Recover as Hormuz Attacks Mount
cards.body: Brent trades at {BRENT}. Kpler said on 24 November that Gulf producers other than Iran exported just under 14 million barrels a day in September and October, about their pre-war level, with Saudi Arabia and the UAE above it. The risk sits on the ships: about 10 tankers have been reported struck near Hormuz since 16 November, the IMO counts 25 seafarers dead, and insurer The Swedish Club advises avoiding the strait. OPEC+ meets on 29 November.

cards.title: Crypto: EU Proposes Curbs on Russian Sanctions Evasion
cards.body: Bitcoin trades at {BTC} and Ether at {ETH}. On 23 November the European Commission proposed a 22nd sanctions package on Russia that targets cryptocurrency used to get around sanctions, alongside measures on sport and visas, Kyiv Independent reports. It is a proposal: it needs unanimous approval from member states, which some officials hope for before the end of the year. Until it is adopted, it does not change the speed or path of Russia's sanctioned payments.

cards.title: Gold: No War-Linked Driver Found
cards.body: Gold trades at {GOLD}. This run's research found no report tying gold's move to the war in the 12-15 November window. The card's last dated check is from 18 September, when gold was $4,364.46 an ounce at 9 a.m. New York time (CNBC), flat while Brent swung. Inference, not a sourced finding: gold appears to be tracking real yields and the cost of holding it rather than escalation risk.
